title: Smartphone Assessment: composition, cohorts and uncertainty

steps.title: Check why Table 1 was accepted
steps.question: What kind of measurement does Gate recognize?
steps.look: Gate accepts polymeric and metallic composition fractions for the phone and its components, grouped by manufacturing era.
steps.boundary: Composition is not recovery efficiency. Gate approval alone does not verify every extracted fact.

steps.title: Read value and uncertainty from one cell
steps.question: What does 58.37 ± 2.11 represent?
steps.look: The casing polymer fraction is split into value 58.37 and uncertainty 2.11. Its header supplies percent and Manufacturing before 2015.
steps.boundary: The ± term is retained as reported; the demo does not infer its statistical definition. Click the highlighted cell for reverse navigation.

steps.title: Inspect Table 2's concentration unit
steps.question: Is 101 ± 28 a percentage?
steps.look: The Ag row supplies ppm. The extracted phone concentration is value 101, uncertainty 28; the bef header becomes the archived condition before.
steps.boundary: Bef/aft refer to manufacturing cohorts, not before/after treatment. The archived short condition is preserved, not silently expanded.

steps.title: Check Table 3's explicit cell unit
steps.question: Does a percentage header override 61 ppm?
steps.look: The whole-phone Ag cell explicitly says 61 ppm. Extraction keeps ppm despite the generic Concentration (%) header; other columns report component mass distributions.
steps.boundary: Whole-device concentration and element distribution across components have different denominators. Neither is process recovery.

steps.title: Attach scope: identify the study population
steps.question: Does this observation describe a named phone model?
steps.look: After document merge and revision, Scope adds source context. Scope describes 30 smartphones from nine brands, grouped by manufacturing year before and after 2015. No model was repeated.
steps.boundary: This is batch evidence, not a measurement for a named catalog model. The Scope description is an archived summary. Scope is post-merge provenance, not an upstream extraction input.

steps.title: Follow the cell into the final relation
steps.question: What survives normalization?
steps.look: Casings becomes casing. The final CONTAINS relation retains 58.37%, uncertainty 2.11, its manufacturing cohort and source cell.
steps.boundary: Entity normalization does not turn a batch observation into a model specification or a pooled estimate.

steps.title: Keep the second cohort separate
steps.question: Should the same endpoints be deduplicated?
steps.look: The after-2015 casing result is 55.69 ± 4.14%. It shares endpoints with the previous result but has a different cohort and cell.
steps.boundary: Shared subject, relation and object do not make these measurements duplicates. This guide makes no statistical significance claim.

steps.title: Trace the batch observation from the graph
steps.question: Can we return to the original concentration cell?
steps.look: Open the phone's Ag CONTAINS observations, choose 101 ppm, then View evidence in replay. Table 2's extraction retains uncertainty 28 and the exact cell.
steps.boundary: This fused record has no separate uncertainty field; its source anchor retains 101±28. Sharing a phone node does not merge cohorts or identify one physical device.
